state.actual_english_lesson:
--- title: Your First Independent Reproducible Project description: Combine functions, modules, files, environments and tests from requirements; verify persistence, rejected-data preservation and clean recovery, then implement an unguided variation. --- import { getProjectExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. This is not another framework scaffold to copy You now know values, containers, control flow, functions, exceptions, modules, files, environments and plain automated tests. Combine those capabilities: **start with requirements and acceptance, implement independently, then compare responsibilities with a reference.** You may consult earlier chapters and official documentation instead of memorizing every API. The deliverable is a local task application, not a Web backend or production persistence system. It is small enough to trace every data change while still requiring real input contracts, file-failure behavior, environment recovery, tests and a changed requirement. Databases, authorization and deployment retain their later dedicated teaching. | Contract | Scope | | --- | --- | | Prerequisites | L07 files/JSON, L08 environments, L09 plain tests, earlier language/module foundations | | Deliverable | Multi-file application, run instructions, declaration/lock, success and failure checks | | Independent acceptance | Empty-directory implementation, second-directory recovery, corrupt-data preservation and an unguided variation | | Not introduced | Web, databases, class design, decorators, async or custom context protocols | The [L10 reference project and inputs](/learning-assets/js2py/u10-local-project.zip) are available for comparison, but **start your own empty directory outside the download**. References are folded below. Verified baseline on 2026-09-28: CPython 3.13.15, uv 0.12.13 and pytest 8.4.2. Business execution uses only the standard library. ## 2. Specify the data and behavior before coding The file contains one JSON array. Each item has exactly title, minutes and done. Title is non-whitespace str with spelling preserved; minutes is an ordinary nonnegative int, rejecting bool, float and numeric strings; done is bool only. Empty arrays, zero minutes and duplicate titles are valid. Preserve order and reject missing/extra fields. Only a **missing** destination initializes this data. An existing empty array is not absence: {getProjectExample('fixtures/initial.json')} Every successful run marks all unfinished tasks whose title exactly equals Read as done. Already-complete items do not increase changed. Save once, then report changed count, total tasks and unfinished minutes. Titles are not unique IDs; matching duplicates are all processed rather than silently adopting a first-match rule. A missing file and a damaged existing file are different events. Invalid encoding, malformed JSON or invalid business shape must produce a visible nonzero failure while preserving the original bytes. Do not initialize, save an empty array or merely warn and continue. Permission and unknown I/O errors cannot become “a new user with no tasks.” ## 3. Separate responsibilities along data flow Draw the flow: **path → open file → parsed text → validated data → business change → summary → serialization → save → display**. At each boundary ask who guarantees input and who interprets or propagates failure. - Validation returns a fresh list of fresh dictionaries. Mutating the result must not mutate the original input. - Rules complete tasks and compute summaries without opening files, printing or creating directories. There is no global mutable task database. - Storage reads/writes and validates. Load propagates absence instead of choosing initialization policy. Save validates/serializes before a destructive open. - The app chooses its owned fixed path, creates its parent, decides when initialization is allowed, orders calls and stops after damaged input. These are ordinary modules/functions, not an invitation to memorize enterprise architecture terms. Equivalent names are fine if responsibilities remain explainable. A small program still must not read or write user files merely on import; more directories do not automatically establish better boundaries. Write your module sketch and each function's inputs, outputs and errors before opening the reference. Type annotations are not required until their dedicated L11 lesson. ## 4. Make the environment explainable too Use this declaration shape with your own project name. Do not bring the reference's installed environment into your implementation: {getProjectExample('pyproject.toml')} {getProjectExample('.python-version')} ```bash uv lock uv sync --locked uv run --locked python -m pytest -q ``` No third-party runtime dependency is a valid choice. Do not force an ecosystem package into a problem the standard library already solves. Pytest remains in dev, with tool dependencies that still need a recoverable lock. Generate the lock from your own declaration, then synchronize in locked mode. Before you write tests, the final command may report no tests; L09 taught why this is not acceptance. Record that state and add real checks. The reference download already has a lock, so restore it with sync --locked rather than silently updating a mismatch first. Do not edit lock internals manually. Empty-directory recovery includes source, declaration, lock, version selection and required fixtures. Caches, personal secrets and real user data have different ownership and recovery responsibilities. ## 5. Define acceptance before implementing First and second process runs should respectively print: ```text Source: new file Changed: 1 Tasks: 3 Pending minutes: 35 ``` ```text Source: existing file Changed: 0 Tasks: 3 Pending minutes: 35 ``` Use fresh Python processes. Retaining a list in one process does not demonstrate persistence. Changed becoming zero follows this particular completion operation's contract; it does not mean every repeated program run is universally side-effect free. Also verify: | Situation | Required observation | | --- | --- | | Import app/storage | Only the probe's output; no directory creation, data I/O or business entry | | Existing empty array | Remains empty; counts and minutes are zero | | Duplicate Read titles, some already done | All match, but count only newly completed items | | Change Practice to 36 minutes | A new process reports 36 rather than hard-coded 35 | | Malformed JSON, invalid encoding or shape | Visible failure, unchanged original bytes, no success report | | Missing parent | App creates its owned parent; storage does not silently create arbitrary directories | | Different cwd | Same anchored project data, no accidental second dataset under the caller | Invalid values rejected before saving must preserve the old file. **A failure during writing can still damage it.** Retain L07's explicit limits instead of turning with, tests or one-document formatting into a database transaction claim. ## 6. Give file tests their own disposable directory Tests must not damage your working task file, and fixture knowledge is not a prerequisite. Introduce one small standard-library utility: TemporaryDirectory creates an owned temporary directory; leaving its with scope cleans up that directory and contents on normal or exceptional exit. {getProjectExample('demo_resource.py')} ```bash uv run --locked python demo_resource.py ``` ```text Inside: True After: False ``` Directory is a string path; Path turns it into the familiar object. Create only test-owned files beneath that temporary directory, never supply a real user's location. After exit, the path name still exists but the location is cleaned up, extending L07's distinction between a name and an available resource. Each file test creates its own directory. A reader need not know it is being tested: it accepts a Path. Similarly, main(path) can accept a test-owned location while the normal entry chooses its fixed default. This is an ordinary function parameter, not premature framework dependency injection or a security promise for arbitrary uploaded paths. ## 7. Work in observable stages rather than one large leap Use small verifiable steps while deciding the implementation yourself: 1. Build pure validation/rules and plain tests for empty, zero, duplicates and non-mutation. 2. Add storage and round-trip in temporary directories; two saves still produce one document. 3. Add orchestration and the fixed path; verify first/repeated/existing-empty behavior. 4. Copy bad input into an owned disposable destination and compare bytes before/after failure; never repair fixtures in place. 5. Use an outer entry from another cwd and probe imports without business execution. 6. Recover in a second clean directory, rerun the whole acceptance table, then attempt the variation. For a red step, identify its layer before changing Python, registries, JSON and assertions simultaneously. Run focused checks after each small change and the complete suite afterward, preserving explainable progress. ## 8. Reference implementation: inspect responsibilities
Complete application reference — after your module sketch and first acceptance Files below are package initialization, validation, rules, storage, app, import probe and outer entry, in that order. Keep the downloaded paths; package-internal files are not arbitrary standalone commands: {getProjectExample('task_app/__init__.py')} {getProjectExample('task_app/validation.py')} {getProjectExample('task_app/rules.py')} {getProjectExample('task_app/storage.py')} {getProjectExample('task_app/app.py')} {getProjectExample('check_import.py')} {getProjectExample('run_tasks.py')} ```bash uv sync --locked uv run --locked python check_import.py uv run --locked python -m task_app.app uv run --locked python -m task_app.app ``` Main(path=None) selects the default only when no test path is supplied. App owns parent creation and the explicit missing-file recovery policy; load_tasks itself continues to propagate absence. Validation returns fresh data, so rule mutation cannot contaminate the caller. The app calculates its summary before saving and prints successful counts only after saving succeeds. Bad inputs fail first; write failures remain visible, and no atomicity guarantee has appeared. Title matching is not a general CRUD, user-ID or authorization system. From the downloaded reference root, enter its parent, explicitly select the project and run the outer entry, then return. --project selects the project without changing the caller's working directory, so the script path is also relative to that parent. Expect the repeated-run output, with no second _output in the parent. For your own renamed project, adjust both directory names rather than patching sys.path. ```bash cd .. uv run --project u10-local-project --locked python u10-local-project/run_tasks.py cd u10-local-project ```
## 9. Reference tests: business and file evidence are different
Open reference tests — after writing your expectation matrix {getProjectExample('tests/test_rules.py')} {getProjectExample('tests/test_storage.py')} ```bash uv run --locked python -m pytest -q uv run --locked python -m pytest --collect-only -q ``` The main suite has **15 cases**, not the 17 obtained by adding the separate solution tests. The first covers current requirements; select variation tests explicitly after attempting the new requirement. Tests use owned temporary directories, never the app's live _output/tasks.json. A cache does not preserve correctness after source or expectations change. Beyond round-trip equality, checks verify independent results, one-document replacement, pre-save rejection without truncation/creation, and original bytes preserved after damaged input. Merely asserting an exception cannot prove data was not already destroyed. Main accepts a test path without fixtures or mocks. Fresh-process and other-cwd acceptance remain additional checks: calling main twice within a test process alone does not prove restart persistence. Keep these types of evidence distinct.
## 10. Diagnose damaged data instead of deleting the evidence Two supplied bad inputs are: {getProjectExample('fixtures/broken.json')} {getProjectExample('fixtures/wrong-shape.json')} In a disposable project copy, first create normal output and preserve a backup. Copy a bad fixture to that copy's _output/tasks.json. Run the same entry, observe nonzero failure, then compare the destination with the injected bytes using an editor or familiar read_bytes. Original fixtures remain unchanged. The first is invalid JSON; the second parses but violates the array-root contract. Neither permits initialization. After observing failure, deliberately restore the good backup and rerun. Deleting damaged data until the app starts is not successful corruption handling. Data recovery, code repair and fresh initialization are different actions. Likewise, do not reinterpret PermissionError as an empty list or broadly relax system permissions to make a demo work. Unknown failures should remain diagnosable instead of producing a misleading successful new file. ## 11. Independent variation: choose a plan within a budget No line-by-line recipe: add a pure function over valid tasks and an ordinary nonnegative int budget. Consider unfinished tasks in original order. Skip an item that does not fit but keep considering later items. Exact fits and zero-minute items are valid. Return fresh selected records plus used minutes; preserve input and perform no file I/O. This is not a globally optimal knapsack algorithm. Do not reorder tasks to maximize packing. First choose a signature and write tests that distinguish break/continue, equality, completed items, bool budgets and shared references. Then implement it, keeping the original 15 tests green.
Variation reference — compare only after your own implementation {getProjectExample('solutions/new_requirement.py')} {getProjectExample('solutions/test_new_requirement.py')} ```bash uv run --locked python -m pytest -q solutions/test_new_requirement.py ``` Two reference tests cover related boundaries but are a starting point, not a comprehensive certificate. Extend them for your implementation. Check continued search after a skip, acceptance of zero, and mutation isolation. Used minutes must come from selected records rather than the entire original input.
## 12. Graduating from this stage is not deployment readiness Exit this stage when you can explain your design from requirements, implement source/environment from an empty directory, detect a deliberate business defect, read data in a fresh process, preserve rejected input, recover in a second directory, complete the variation, and state the remaining concurrency, authorization, transaction and service-operation limits. Your README must specify command working directories, versions, first/repeated outputs, intentional failures, owned output paths and recovery steps. A pause record includes source changes, last test command/count, whether data is currently damaged, backup location and the next behavior to prove—not merely the last page read. L11 adds annotations to functions/containers whose behavior you already understand, separating static checking from runtime validation. Types, models, decorators and resource protocols then prepare HTTP and FastAPI; this integration assignment is not a shortcut past server foundations. ## 13. Sources and reuse boundaries Checked on 2026-09-28: [Python temporary directories](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/tempfile.html#tempfile.TemporaryDirectory), [pathlib](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/pathlib.html), [JSON](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/json.html), [modules/packages](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/modules.html), [pytest assertions](https://docs.pytest.org/en/8.4.x/how-to/assert.html) and [uv synchronization](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/sync/). We reuse explained mechanisms and introduce safe temporary-directory usage, not unexplained fixtures or async resources. A library's ability to perform an operation does not transfer responsibility for data recovery, trust boundaries or deployment to that library.

actual_download_files.task_app/storage.py:
import json

from .validation import validate_tasks


def load_tasks(path):
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        value = json.load(stream)
    return validate_tasks(value)


def save_tasks(path, value):
    tasks = validate_tasks(value)
    text = json.dumps(tasks, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as stream:
        stream.write(text + "\n")
actual_download_files.task_app/app.py:
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .rules import complete_title, summarize
from .storage import load_tasks, save_tasks


def initial_tasks():
    return [
        {"title": "Read", "minutes": 20, "done": False},
        {"title": "Practice", "minutes": 35, "done": False},
        {"title": "Review", "minutes": 0, "done": True},
    ]


def main(path=None):
    if path is None:
        path = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "_output" / "tasks.json"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        tasks = load_tasks(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Source: new file")
        tasks = initial_tasks()
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
        print("Invalid existing data; refusing to save")
        raise
    else:
        print("Source: existing file")
    result, changed = complete_title(tasks, "Read")
    summary = summarize(result)
    save_tasks(path, result)
    print("Changed:", changed)
    print("Tasks:", summary["count"])
    print("Pending minutes:", summary["pending_minutes"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
actual_download_files.tests/test_rules.py:
import pytest
from task_app.app import initial_tasks
from task_app.rules import complete_title, summarize
from task_app.validation import validate_tasks


def test_normal_completion_and_summary():
    result, changed = complete_title(initial_tasks(), "Read")
    assert changed == 1
    assert result[0]["done"] is True
    assert summarize(result) == {"count": 3, "pending_minutes": 35}


def test_zero_empty_and_no_matching_title():
    assert summarize([]) == {"count": 0, "pending_minutes": 0}
    assert complete_title([], "Read") == ([], 0)
    tasks = [{"title": "Zero", "minutes": 0, "done": False}]
    result, changed = complete_title(tasks, "Absent")
    assert changed == 0 and result == tasks
    assert summarize(result)["pending_minutes"] == 0


def test_every_duplicate_matches_but_only_new_changes_count():
    tasks = [
        {"title": "Read", "minutes": 1, "done": False},
        {"title": "Read", "minutes": 2, "done": True},
        {"title": "Read", "minutes": 3, "done": False},
    ]
    result, changed = complete_title(tasks, "Read")
    assert changed == 2
    assert summarize(result)["pending_minutes"] == 0
    repeated, changed_again = complete_title(result, "Read")
    assert changed_again == 0 and repeated == result


def test_input_and_returned_records_do_not_share_mutation():
    source = initial_tasks()
    result, changed = complete_title(source, "Read")
    assert changed == 1 and source == initial_tasks()
    result[1]["minutes"] = 999
    assert source[1]["minutes"] == 35


def test_strict_shape_and_types():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks({"tasks": []})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks([{"title": "Read", "minutes": True, "done": False}])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks([{"title": "Read", "minutes": 20, "done": 0}])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks([{"title": "Read", "minutes": -1, "done": False}])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks([{"title": "Read", "minutes": "20", "done": False}])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        validate_tasks([{"title": "Read", "minutes": 20, "done": False, "extra": 1}])


def test_title_spelling_and_invalid_selection():
    tasks = [{"title": " Read ", "minutes": 20, "done": False}]
    result, changed = complete_title(tasks, "Read")
    assert changed == 0 and result[0]["title"] == " Read "
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        complete_title(tasks, "   ")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        complete_title(tasks, None)
actual_download_files.tests/test_storage.py:
import json
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import pytest
from task_app.app import initial_tasks, main
from task_app.storage import load_tasks, save_tasks


def test_round_trip_and_independent_results():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        source = [{"title": "学习", "minutes": 0, "done": False}]
        save_tasks(path, source)
        loaded = load_tasks(path)
        assert loaded == source
        loaded[0]["title"] = "changed"
        assert load_tasks(path) == source
        assert "学习" in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        assert path.read_bytes().endswith(b"\n")


def test_missing_file_propagates():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "absent.json"
        with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
            load_tasks(path)
        assert not path.exists()


def test_rejected_save_does_not_truncate_existing_file():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        save_tasks(path, initial_tasks())
        before = path.read_bytes()
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            save_tasks(path, {"tasks": []})
        assert path.read_bytes() == before


def test_rejected_save_does_not_create_missing_file():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            save_tasks(path, [None])
        assert not path.exists()


def test_repeated_save_is_one_document_not_append():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        save_tasks(path, initial_tasks())
        save_tasks(path, [])
        assert path.read_bytes() == b"[]\n"
        assert load_tasks(path) == []


def test_main_first_and_second_and_empty_runs():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "nested" / "tasks.json"
        main(path)
        first = path.read_bytes()
        assert load_tasks(path)[0]["done"] is True
        main(path)
        assert path.read_bytes() == first
        save_tasks(path, [])
        main(path)
        assert path.read_bytes() == b"[]\n"


def test_main_does_not_overwrite_malformed_json():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        path.write_bytes(b"{broken\n")
        with pytest.raises(json.JSONDecodeError):
            main(path)
        assert path.read_bytes() == b"{broken\n"


def test_main_does_not_overwrite_invalid_encoding():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        path.write_bytes(b"\xff")
        with pytest.raises(UnicodeDecodeError):
            main(path)
        assert path.read_bytes() == b"\xff"


def test_main_does_not_overwrite_invalid_business_data():
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="js2py-test-") as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "tasks.json"
        path.write_text('{"tasks": []}\n', encoding="utf-8")
        before = path.read_bytes()
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            main(path)
        assert path.read_bytes() == before

import pytest

from solutions.new_requirement import plan_within_budget


def test_order_skip_and_later_fit():
    tasks = [
        {"title": "Large", "minutes": 50, "done": False},
        {"title": "Fit", "minutes": 20, "done": False},
        {"title": "Zero", "minutes": 0, "done": False},
        {"title": "Done", "minutes": 1, "done": True},
    ]
    selected, used = plan_within_budget(tasks, 20)
    assert [task["title"] for task in selected] == ["Fit", "Zero"]
    assert used == 20
    selected[0]["done"] = True
    assert tasks[1]["done"] is False


def test_empty_zero_and_rejections():
    assert plan_within_budget([], 0) == ([], 0)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        plan_within_budget([], True)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        plan_within_budget([], -1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        plan_within_budget([None], 20)
